As the race toward the 2027 Bauchi State governorship election gathers momentum, political debates are becoming louder across the state. One issue that has recently dominated discussions is the controversy surrounding the academic qualifications of the Allied People’s Movement (APM) governorship candidate, Hon. Yakubu Adamu. The issue has generated heated arguments on social media, radio programmes and in newspapers. While public scrutiny is a healthy part of democracy, it is equally important that such discussions are guided by facts, fairness and respect for the rule of law. Nigeria’s Constitution is clear about the educational qualification required to contest the office of Governor. It sets out the minimum constitutional requirement, and where questions arise about a candidate’s eligibility, the appropriate institutions and the courts have the responsibility to interpret and apply the law. Public opinion should never replace due process. Advertisement There is a clear difference between raising legitimate questions and reaching conclusions before the competent authorities have completed their work. Democracy is built on justice, and justice requires evidence, fairness and the right of every individual to be heard. However, beyond this controversy lies a much bigger question: Is this the most important issue facing the people of Bauchi State today? Across our communities, families are struggling with the high cost of living. Many young people remain unemployed despite having qualifications. Farmers are worried about insecurity and the rising cost of agricultural inputs. Parents are concerned about the quality of education available to their children, while many communities continue to face serious challenges in accessing quality healthcare. Advertisement These are the issues that directly affect the lives of ordinary people every day. As citizens, we should ask every governorship candidate practical questions. What is your plan to create jobs? How will you improve education? What solutions do you have for insecurity? How will you strengthen agriculture and support farmers? What will you do differently to improve healthcare, roads and economic opportunities? These questions are far more important than allowing ourselves to become consumed by political controversies that are yet to be conclusively determined by the appropriate authorities. Yakubu Adamu, like every other candidate seeking public office, should be evaluated by the people based on his vision, competence, leadership qualities and proposed solutions to the problems confronting Bauchi State. Every candidate deserves equal treatment under the law and equal opportunity to present his or her ideas before the electorate. The media also has a critical responsibility in this process. Investigative journalism is one of the pillars of democracy because it promotes transparency and accountability. However, this responsibility must always be exercised with professionalism, accuracy and fairness. Reports should be balanced, verified and should avoid creating the impression that allegations are already established facts before the legal process has run its course. At the same time, politicians and their supporters should remain peaceful and respect democratic institutions. Political competition should never divide our people or distract us from our common desire for a better Bauchi State. Gov Bala declares zero tolerance for violent crimes in Bauchi. Bauchi State Governor, Bala Abdulkadir Mohammed , has declared that perpetrators of violent crimes anywhere in the state will have no hiding place, as the government intensifies efforts to safeguard the lives and property of innocent, law-abiding citizens. The Governor made the declaration during a condolence visit to the family of late Rilwanu Dauda, who was stabbed to death by political thugs over campaign billboards and posters of a political party and candidate in Karofin-Madaki within Bauchi metropolis. Bala Mohammed reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to maintaining law and order across the state in order to safeguard the lives and property of innocent citizens. He described the incident as a tragic loss and assured the bereaved family that justice would be pursued without fear or favour but through due process, and that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law. The Governor noted that while Bauchi State has continued to intensify efforts to combat banditry and other security threats affecting some rural communities, his administration is equally determined to address criminal activities within the state capital and other urban areas to guarantee the safety of all residents. He called on citizens to remain law-abiding and avoid resorting to violence in resolving disputes, urging members of the public to cooperate with security agencies by providing credible information that would aid ongoing investigations and strengthen crime prevention efforts. The Governor also prayed for the repose of the soul of the deceased, asking Almighty Allah to forgive his shortcomings, grant him Aljannatul Firdaus, and give his family the strength and patience to bear the painful loss. He assured them that the government would not relent in ensuring that those responsible for the killing, and anyone connected to it, are apprehended and made to face the law. Responding on behalf of the family, a representative of the late Rilwanu thanked the Governor for the visit and for the support extended to them in their moment of grief. The Governor was accompanied on the condolence visit by top government officials and other stakeholders, who joined him in offering prayers for the late Rilwanu Dauda and expressing the Bauchi State Government’s sympathy with the bereaved family. In the same vein, the governorship candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) in Bauchi State, Dr. Yakubu Adamu, paid a condolence visit to the bereaved family, expressing sympathy over the loss and praying for Allah to grant him repose. During the visit, Adamu condemned the incident, describing it as unfortunate and unacceptable, and assured the family that justice must prevail. He stressed the need for the authorities to ensure that those responsible are identified and prosecuted in accordance with the law. Recall that yet-to-be-arrested individuals, believed to be political thugs, allegedly stabbed Ustaz Ridwan (Rilwanu) Dauda, a resident of Karofin-Madaki, around the JEDCO transformer in Bauchi metropolis, to death. Reports from the area indicate that the incident occurred on Sunday following a heated argument with the thugs over the posting of a politician’s poster on a building. A resident of the area told our correspondent that the late Ridwan had told a man not to paste the poster on the wall of their building, but the man refused and insisted on doing so. It was further gathered that the political thug called a colleague who came to the scene and proceeded to paste the poster, resulting in a heated argument. The resident said it was at that point that one of the thugs brought out a dagger, stabbed the late Ridwan in the chest, and fled. 2027 : Bauchi PDP rejects alliance with APM , dismisses rival faction. The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Bauchi State has rejected any alliance or collaboration with the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), dismissing the reported merger of a rival faction of the party into the APM. The PDP State Chairman, Ibrahim Kashim Toro, stated this on Tuesday while addressing journalists at the party’s secretariat along Maiduguri Road in Bauchi. Toro said the faction that announced the move to the APM was no longer part of the legitimate PDP in the state, alleging that its members had been expelled before the latest development. “As you can see, every member of the PDP is here, there is no other PDP anywhere in Bauchi State. Those who left are not legitimate members of the PDP because they had been expelled long before now,” he said. He maintained that his faction remained the authentic PDP in Bauchi State, citing various court judgments in support of its position. The chairman said the party had fielded candidates for all elective positions ahead of the 2027 general elections, adding that their names had been uploaded on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) portal. “We are the PDP and we have fielded candidates for all elective offices in the 2027 general elections. INEC has since uploaded our candidates on its portal as displayed,” he said. Toro said the PDP would participate fully in the 2027 elections and disclosed that the party would soon commence its statewide campaign. He urged party members across the state to disregard the announcement by the rival faction and intensify mobilisation for the party’s candidates ahead of the elections. The party’s Legal Adviser, Yahaya Garkuwa, also maintained that the Toro-led faction was the authentic PDP in the state, citing various court judgments in support of the position. He said the party remained intact in Bauchi State and had no plan to join or collaborate with the APM.

PDP denies collapse into APM , threatens legal action. BAUCHI — THE Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Bauchi State has dismissed reports that its structure has collapsed into the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), describing the claim as false and alleging that it was being spread by individuals impersonating party officials. The party’s Legal Adviser in the state, Yahaya Garkuwa, stated this on Tuesday at a press conference held at the PDP secretariat along Maiduguri Bypass, Bauchi. Garkuwa said the PDP recognised by law in Bauchi State remained the faction led by Hon. Ibrahim Kashim Toro, while the national leadership was headed by Abdulrahman Mohammed. He said the leadership dispute within the party had been the subject of several court cases, adding that successive judicial pronouncements had affirmed the leadership structure backed by the Bauchi PDP. According to him, the Federal High Court affirmed the Abdulrahman Mohammed-led caretaker committee as the authentic national leadership of the party. He said the faction led by Tanimu Turaki subsequently appealed the judgment, but the Court of Appeal upheld the leadership of Mohammed at the national level and that of Ibrahim Kashim Toro in Bauchi State. “Dissatisfied with the decision, the Tanimu Turaki faction went to the Court of Appeal where the Appeal Court still confirmed the leadership of the PDP under Abdulrahman Mohammed, and in Bauchi State under Hon. Ibrahim’s leadership,” Garkuwa said. He added that the matter was eventually taken to the Supreme Court, which, according to him, ruled in favour of the faction led by Mohammed. “At the Supreme Court, judgment was given in our favour where the Supreme Court said the Tanimu Turaki faction is not known by law, that only the PDP under Abdulrahman Mohammed is known by law, while here in Bauchi State, the PDP known by law is the one under Honourable Ibrahim,” he said. Garkuwa alleged that members of the rival faction had resorted to impersonation and the spread of what he described as false information after exhausting their legal options. “Now that they don’t have anywhere to go by the judgment of the Supreme Court, they now started impersonating that they are leaders of the PDP. And as they don’t have where to stay, they decided to create confusion to tell the public that the PDP structure has collapsed into APM,” he said. The legal adviser insisted that the PDP had neither joined the APM nor any other political party, saying the party remained intact. “We, the authentic members of the PDP, are still in the PDP. We have not joined any other political party; we still remain in the PDP,” he added. Garkuwa further disclosed that the Bauchi State PDP leadership was preparing to take legal action against individuals allegedly parading themselves as officials of the party. He urged members of the public to disregard reports of the party’s alleged collapse, insisting that the PDP recognised by law remained under the current state leadership. “You can see that we are the only PDP members whose candidates’ names were published by INEC ahead of the 2027 general elections,” he said. He also challenged the rival faction to produce evidence of the candidates it intended to field under the PDP platform. “If they are truly members of the PDP, let them name their candidates. They don’t have candidates,” Garkuwa said. He assured party supporters that the PDP remained politically active in the state and was preparing for the 2027 general elections. “PDP is not collapsing into any political party. PDP is still standing, PDP is still strong and is fully prepared for the 2027 general elections,” he said. The press conference was attended by the state PDP chairman, other party officials, stakeholders and supporters. 2027 : APM Names Ibrahim Bala as Running Mate to Makinde for Presidential Election - Latest News In Nigeria , Nigeria News Today , Your Online Nigerian Newspaper. The Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM) has officially named Ibrahim Adamu Bala as the running mate to its presidential candidate, Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Details published on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) candidate nomination portal confirmed Bala’s nomination. At 51, Bala hails from Bauchi State, giving the party a South-North presidential ticket. A senior APM official, speaking on condition of anonymity, explained that Makinde had completed the submission of his nomination with Bala as his vice-presidential candidate. “You cannot submit your presidential nomination without a running mate. The nomination has been filed,” the source said. The official dismissed speculation linking the choice to Bauchi State Governor Bala Mohammed, clarifying that the vice-presidential candidate is Ibrahim Adamu Bala, not Mohammed. “There is no connection at all. They only have similar names. The running mate is Ibrahim Adamu Bala, not Bala Mohammed. I laughed when I saw the report because I knew people would confuse the two,” the source added. Makinde, currently serving his second and final term as governor of Oyo State, declared his presidential ambition on May 14 at a joint rally organised by his faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the APM at Mapo Hall in Ibadan. The declaration followed a Memorandum of Understanding signed between the PDP faction and the APM at the PDP South-West Zonal Secretariat. On May 30, Makinde formally accepted the APM presidential ticket, pledging to tackle insecurity, unemployment, hunger, and the rising cost of living if elected. He also promised to decentralise Nigeria’s security architecture, granting states greater powers to address local challenges. The confirmation of Bala’s nomination on the INEC portal cements the Makinde-Bala ticket, positioning the APM to contest the presidency with a South-North balance as the 2027 general elections draw closer.

Breaking : APM sweeps 20 chairmanship seats in Bauchi LG poll , wins 319 councillorship seats. August 17, 2026 Adejayan Gbenga Breaking News , Politics 0 The Allied Peoples Movement (APM) has won all 20 chairmanship seats contested in the Bauchi State local government elections held on Monday. The results were announced by the Bauchi State Independent Electoral Commission (BASIEC) on Monday night after the completion of voting, counting, collation and verification across the state. The chairperson of BASIEC, Hon. Hajiya Jummai S. Abubakar, declared all 20 APM candidates winners of the chairmanship elections in their respective local government areas. She said the declaration followed the successful completion of all electoral processes and verification of the results. “Following the conclusion of voting, counting, collation and verification, I, Hon. Hajiya Jummai S. Abubakar (Gimbiyar Dass), Chairperson of BASIEC, hereby declared that all 20 APM candidates emerged victorious as Chairmen of the respective Local Government Areas,” she said. In Alkaleri Local Government Area, Bappah Aliyu Mohammed emerged victorious with 107,482 votes, while Umar Mohammed Aliyu won Bauchi LGA with 125,170 votes. Zakka Luka Magaji secured victory in Bogoro LGA with 25,282 votes, while Iliya Isah won Dambam with 19,730 votes. Ya’u Samaila Sade emerged winner in Darazo with 67,276 votes, while Mohammed Abubakar Jibo won Dass with 35,264 votes. Other winners declared by BASIEC included Ali Babayo, who secured Gamawa LGA with 54,423 votes, and Mohammed Idris M, who won Ganjuwa with 24,150 votes. Mustapha Alhaji Musa emerged victorious in Giade with 33,864 votes, while Dankawuwa Ya’u won Itas/Gadau with 24,989 votes. In Jama’are, Inuwa Abdullahi secured victory with 36,766 votes. Yusuf Babayo Zaki won Katagum with 65,626 votes, while Garba Musa emerged victorious in Kirfi with 24,787 votes. Salisu Hussaini won Misau with 34,378 votes, while Yahuza Adamu Haruna secured Ningi with 29,387 votes. In Shira LGA, former majority leader of the Bauchi State House of Assembly, Saleh Hodi Jibir, polled 37,135 votes to emerge winner. Sama’ila Wakili Lere won Tafawa Balewa with 46,625 votes, while Abubakar Ibrahim Dembo secured victory in Toro with 109,999 votes. Habibu Idris Usman won Warji with 43,066 votes, while Mas’ud Aliyu emerged winner in Zaki with 19,984 votes. The APM also recorded a dominant performance in the councillorship elections, winning 319 of the 323 ward seats contested across Bauchi State. BASIEC said the remaining four seats were shared among four political parties. The Social Democratic Party (SDP) won Dandango Ward in Bauchi LGA, while the National Rescue Movement (NRM) secured Darazo South Ward in Darazo LGA. The Zenith Labour Party (ZLP) won Wandi Ward in Dass LGA, while the Young Progressive Party (YPP) secured Zirami Ward in Giade LGA. The electoral commission said the successful candidates had been duly confirmed as elected after satisfying the applicable legal requirements and securing the highest valid votes in their respective constituencies. The BASIEC chairperson maintained that the elections were conducted independently and in accordance with the law. She also commended Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed Abdulkadir, for his support to the commission during the conduct of the local government elections. Abubakar congratulated the people of Bauchi State and all candidates who emerged victorious in the elections. With the declaration, the APM has secured all 20 chairmanship positions in Bauchi State and 319 of the 323 councillorship seats contested in the local government elections.

Airport project: Oyo did not get N50bn from Tinubu, Makinde replies Wike. Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has denied claims by Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, that President Bola Tinubu gave the state N50 billion to upgrade the Ladoke Akintola International Airport, Ibadan. Makinde spoke on Tuesday while addressing supporters at the Makinde/Daura 2027 Presidential Town Hall meeting in Katsina. He said the Oyo State Government did not receive N50 billion from the Federal Government, adding that the airport upgrade was being funded entirely by the state. Wike had made the claim on Monday while appearing on TVC’s Journalists’ Hangout programme. Makinde said, “The President did not give me or Oyo State N50 billion to upgrade the Ibadan Airport. The Ibadan Airport upgrade project is being undertaken 100 per cent with the funds of Oyo State.” On the transfer of presidential power, Makinde said he would transmit power to the Vice President whenever he is unavailable if elected president in 2027. He said he would obey Section 145 of the Constitution, which requires the President to transmit a written declaration to the Senate President and Speaker of the House of Representatives when proceeding on vacation or otherwise unable to perform the functions of office. “I promise you that, as your President, I will follow the Constitution to the letter. If I am not going to be available, if I am on vacation, I will transmit power to the Vice President. Record this and hold me accountable,” he said. Makinde also promised to establish reliable data on out-of-school children and develop measures to return them to school. He called for mining to be removed from the Exclusive Legislative List and devolved to the states, while the Federal Government retains oversight. On 2027 election, he urged Nigerians to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the poll. Earlier, APM vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, said the North-West and Nigeria were “yearning for a reset”, citing insecurity and poverty as major challenges facing the region. Daura said Makinde’s proposed agenda aligned with his call for fundamental change and urged supporters to exercise their civic rights.
